item.description:
Rein 0.9.4

  • System EQ is back. A macOS update had silently broken the system-wide equalizer (the audio

tap it relied on started returning silence). The EQ now captures the system mix the same proven

way per-app audio does, so shaping your whole output works again. If an app starts playing while

the EQ is on, it joins within a second.

  • Licence-clean ffmpeg. The bundled ffmpeg is now our own LGPL build — hardware VideoToolbox

H.264 encoding (which casting already used) and native decoders, with the licence text and source

reference shipped in the app. No user-visible change to casting; very old HDR films may tone-map

with slightly simpler colour handling.

Rein 0.9.3

New: Storage. A GrandPerspective-style view of where your disk space goes, in Rein's tools list.

  • Treemap. Scan Home, Downloads, Desktop, Documents, Movies or Library and get a treemap of

what's using space — biggest things first. Tap a folder to drill in, follow the breadcrumb back,

tap a file to reveal it in Finder.

  • Largest items. A ranked list of the biggest files and folders at whatever level you're viewing,

each with a size bar and a reveal-in-Finder shortcut.

  • Reclaim space, safely. One card surfaces the safe-to-clear piles — app caches, logs, Xcode

DerivedData and simulator caches. Clearing them moves everything to the Trash, never a

permanent delete, so you can always put it back. Rein refuses to touch anything outside those

known-safe locations.

Storage never changes any system setting, so there's nothing to undo — and it needs no privileged

helper. Scans skip folders macOS keeps private; grant Full Disk Access in System Settings ▸ Privacy

for a complete picture.

Main window hardening. Two changes aimed at the "text and graphics bounce right-to-left" glitch

on the Overview: the window no longer runs SwiftUI's extra min/ideal sizing passes (the two widths

the misdrawn content was appearing at), and the status dot's pulse is now self-contained instead of

a window-wide animation transaction. The window's 1040×600 minimum is unchanged.

Rein 0.9.2

Two fixes for the remote Dock, from first field use:

  • Tapping a Dock app now behaves like clicking the real Dock. An app that was running without

any windows (Chrome's background mode) previously activated invisibly — now it opens a fresh

window, and apps that aren't running launch as before.

  • Desktop switching (◀ / ▶ on the phone) actually switches. The keyboard chord is now

synthesized as a real hand would press it — Control key down, arrow, Control up, with the flags

genuine arrow keys carry — which the system's Mission Control layer requires. (Your Mission

Control "Move left/right a space" shortcuts must be enabled in System Settings ▸ Keyboard ▸

Shortcuts — they are by default, even if you normally swipe.)
